newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Bigger EU must have social conscience, leaders say.
newsitem.headline: Bigger EU must have social conscience, leaders say.

text.p: European socialist prime ministers and party leaders said on Sunday an expanded EU must focus more on social policy and not be just a free-trade area.

Leaders of the Party of European Socialists, meeting in Hungary for the first time outside an EU country, also said they wanted negotiations on enlargement to begin simultaneously with all candidate countries six months after the conclusion of the EU's Intergovernmental Conference, due to end next year.
"We have to do it (enlarge the EU)," PES President Rudolf Scharping, the German opposition Social Democrat parliamentary leader, told a news conference ending the two-day meeting in Budapest.
"This is the time to do something and not the time to let it go wrong because of details," Scharping said. Party leaders from 15 EU states and seven non-members also attended.
A declaration issued at the conference said EU enlargement was a "political necessity and a historic opportunity for Europe".
"Without proper preparation, enlargement might lead to a multi-speed Union and one that is no more than a free-trade area," the declaration added.

"That is not our Europe...In Budapest socialists and social democrats from the European Union and the applicant states started the process of cooperation to ensure that our Europe is a Europe of employment and growth, economic and social cohesion, environmental protection and of peace and security for all its citizens."

Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn, whose country is considered one of the front runners along with the Czech Republic and Poland for relatively early admission to the EU, said he recognised the fears of other countries that admitting new members could cost a lot of money.

But he suggested the EU should make reforms during the Intergovernment Conference to free up money now spent on agricultural subsidies and other programmes and to channel those funds into the "reconstruction of the EU".

Jozef Oleksy, leader of Poland's Social Democracy party, said countries wanting to join the EU should be given some say in the proceedings of the EU's Intergovernmental Conference since it would shape the union's future.

"This is not only the question of the members of today of the European Union. This is also our question. We will be members in five years...and we get information about this conference but I am not satisfied," Oleksy said.
"We would like to introduce some ideas and proposals for the internal changes inside the European Union because it will be our structure in the future."
Prime Minister Wim Kok of the Netherlands said one of the purposes of the Budapest conference was to give information to the aspiring EU members, and to solicit their views.

"Of course we always have to make a distinction between the IGC itself which has not only the purpose of enlargement but also the purpose of improving the functioning of the present union," Kok told reporters.

Lionel Jospin, the French Socialist leader narrowly defeated for the presidency last year by Jacques Chirac, said it was reassuring at a time when anti-EU sentiment was sweeping some countries that new countries want to join. "It is good that even in these circumstances people want to join us," Jospin told reporters.
